scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning:
The scenario involves a former roommate who abandoned his belongings after moving out, leaving the narrator with the responsibility to deal with them. The narrator attempted to contact the roommate for two weeks via text and email to arrange pickup or disposal, but received no response. Concerned about potential charges from the landlord for removal, the narrator discarded most items but sold 60 video games to a local store for $600. When confronted later, the roommate demanded reimbursement, but the narrator refused, citing prior unsuccessful attempts to contact him.

Key moral considerations:
- The roommate abandoned his property without making arrangements for its disposition.
- The narrator made reasonable efforts (two weeks of contact attempts) to give the roommate an opportunity to reclaim his belongings.
- The narrator acted to prevent the landlord from incurring removal costs, which could have negatively impacted both parties (e.g., deductions from a security deposit).
- Selling the games was a way to recoup potential costs or losses, but the primary intent seemed to be disposing of abandoned property responsibly.
- The roommate's anger and demand for payment came after he had ignored all communication, suggesting a lack of responsibility on his part.

Morally, the action appears acceptable because:
- The narrator did not act recklessly or maliciously; they tried to resolve the situation amicably.
- The property was abandoned, and the roommate had effectively relinquished his claim by ignoring repeated attempts to contact him.
- Selling the games was a practical solution to avoid waste and potential financial loss, especially since the games had value and could be reused.
- The roommate's subsequent demand seems opportunistic, given his prior inaction.

Thus, the action is morally acceptable.
